paper.title_en: Ground-state phase diagram of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg zigzag ladder with anisotropic $Γ$ term revisited
paper.abstract_en: We study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet with an anisotropic $Γ$ term on a zigzag ladder, which can be exactly mapped to the spin-1/2 XYZ zigzag ladder by a spin rotation. This model has recently attracted considerable interest as an effective model for the quasi-one-dimensional magnetic semiconductor YbCuS$_2$. For the model, the ground-state phase diagram was previously proposed by Saito and Hotta [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 166701 (2024); Phys. Rev. B 110, 024409 (2024)]. We systematically reexamine the phase diagram through complementary numerical and analytical approaches, including exact diagonalization, the density-matrix renormalization group method, and low-energy effective theories. We thereby demonstrate that when the anisotropic $Γ$ term is present, the model exhibits the Néel, dimer, ferromagnetic, and double-Néel phases, all of which have a finite excitation gap. The gapless Tomonaga-Luttinger-liquid (TLL) phase appears only in the isotropic case where the $Γ$ term is absent. We also confirm that the transitions between the Néel and dimer phases and between the Néel and ferromagnetic phases are continuous transitions governed by Gaussian criticality with central charge $c=1$. The TLL parameter characterizing the critical states at the Gaussian transitions is estimated numerically.
